stem: Amit faces South-West. He turns 135 degrees clockwise. Which direction is he now facing?

per_option_rationale.rationale: South-West is 225 degrees from North (measuring clockwise). Adding 135 degrees gives 225 + 135 = 360 degrees = 0 degrees = North.

225 + 135 = 360 but misreading as 360 - 45 = 315 degrees gives North-West, or miscomputing 225 + 135 = 345 gives North-North-West; rounding to North-East reflects a slip landing at 45 degrees instead of 0.
Applying 135 degrees counter-clockwise from South-West: 225 - 135 = 90 degrees = East, confusing the turn direction.

Starting from South-East (135 degrees) instead of South-West (225 degrees) and adding 135 gives 270 = West, or treating South-West as 135 degrees and adding 135 = 270 gives West; adjusting to nearest compass point gives South-East by reversing the starting direction.

explanation: Compass degrees clockwise from North: N=0, NE=45, E=90, SE=135, S=180, SW=225, W=270, NW=315. SW = 225 deg. Add 135 deg clockwise: 225 + 135 = 360 = 0 = North.

explanation_sections.punchline: South-West plus a 135-degree clockwise rotation completes exactly one full circle back to North.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: assign numeric degree to SW (225). Add clockwise rotation (135). Reduce modulo 360: (225+135) mod 360 = 0 = North. This rotation covers SW -> W -> NW -> N.
explanation_sections.lesson: Convert intercardinal starting directions to degree values before applying rotations to avoid turn-direction errors.
explanation_sections.timing: About 60-80 seconds. The trap is applying the turn counter-clockwise (giving East) or misplacing SW at 135 degrees (giving a wrong start).
